scientific_truth: Bulletproof coffee is high in caffeine and fat. Is the hip breakfast substitute a kind of fitness potion? Or is it even harmful? Because there have been no studies on this coffee blend with human test subjects, we cannot make any reliable statements.

claim_subject: Do apples help with smoking cessation?
scientific_truth: Apples contain numerous ingredients and rightly have the reputation of being a healthy snack. Whether they can help to give up cigarettes has not yet been investigated in studies.

claim_subject: Do products made from fenugreek seeds help you lose weight?
scientific_truth: We found only one study in which participants had not lost weight after six weeks. However, the study period is very short, the number of participants small and the quality mediocre. It therefore remains unclear whether fenugreek seeds can help lose weight in the longer term.

claim_subject: Does skipping breakfast increase heart attack risk?
scientific_truth: There is no clear evidence that not eating breakfast could be a cause of obesity and, as a consequence, an increased risk of heart attack. It is possible, however, that it is primarily those people who are overweight and have a higher heart risk who forgo their morning meal.

claim_subject: Does wheat make you fat and sick?
scientific_truth: There is no evidence in current studies that wheat has a special connection with obesity and its consequences. Attributing a special role to wheat seems implausible.

claim_subject: Do whole grains lower the likelihood of dying early?
scientific_truth: People who eat whole grain products instead of foods made from refined flour are likely to live longer and probably have a lower risk of dying from cancer or cardiovascular disease.

claim_subject: Does the consumption of dairy products promote mucus and diseases of the ear, nose and throat?
scientific_truth: There is no scientific evidence to prove that cow's milk causes mucus.

claim_subject: Does regular consumption of energy drinks harm heart health?
scientific_truth: This question is insufficiently researched. Larger studies over a longer period of time are needed to assess the heart risk from energy drinks.

claim_subject: Do light drinks promote obesity?
scientific_truth: Several cohort studies show that people who frequently drink light drinks are more likely to be overweight. However, this does not prove that sweetener drinks make you fat. For it is equally conceivable that overweight people try to lose weight with light drinks. Whether they are successful in doing so is unclear.

claim_subject: Does coffee reduce the risk of dementia?
scientific_truth: One to two cups of coffee a day may protect against mental decline in the long term. It should not be more than that. It is unclear where this effect comes from and whether other caffeinated beverages might also be protective.

claim_subject: Does sugar consumption increase the risk of developing type 2 diabetes regardless of obesity?
scientific_truth: Sugar-containing soft drinks can - if consumed regularly - cause obesity. Obesity, in turn, increases the likelihood of developing type 2 diabetes. However, sugared soft drinks probably also increase the risk of diabetes independently of obesity.

claim_subject: Does a lower salt diet reduce the likelihood of cardiovascular disease?
scientific_truth: A lower-salt diet has been shown to help reduce elevated blood pressure somewhat. It is possible, but not certain, that this reduces the likelihood of dying from a stroke or the consequences of narrowed heart vessels, such as a heart attack.

claim_subject: Is less eaten from red plates?
scientific_truth: In two psychological experiments, participants were less likely to eat salty pretzels, popcorn or chocolate chips if they were served on red plates. It is unclear whether the effect lasts over a longer period of time.

claim_subject: Does red wine protect better against cardiovascular disease than white wine?
scientific_truth: There is evidence that moderate amounts of alcohol may protect against cardiovascular disease, but the effect is not well established. Whether this possibly protective effect is stronger with red wine than with white wine or other alcoholic beverages has not been sufficiently investigated.

claim_subject: Do azo food dyes cause attention deficit disorder and hyperactivity in children?
scientific_truth: Some studies fuel the suspicion that azo dyes can exacerbate ADHD symptoms.

claim_subject: Does turmeric prevent or cure cancer?
scientific_truth: Animal studies provide tentative evidence that turmeric can prevent or treat cancer. Whether turmeric has such an effect in humans cannot be assessed due to the low confidence level of a few studies conducted to date.

claim_subject: Does breastfeeding reduce the risk of sudden infant death syndrome?
scientific_truth: Breastfeeding can possibly reduce the risk of sudden infant death syndrome, but this is not entirely certain. Other factors can also reduce the risk.

claim_subject: Do boron preparations such as borax, boric acid, or calcium fructoborate relieve pain associated with age-related joint wear (osteoarthritis)?
scientific_truth: The few studies on this are of poor quality and therefore not trustworthy. Moreover, there is no evidence that the human body needs boron at all.

claim_subject: Can glutamate in food cause intolerance symptoms?
scientific_truth: There is no conclusive evidence that the consumption of glutamate triggers complaints. However, since studies conducted to date have shown deficiencies, it cannot be ruled out that there are isolated individuals who react sensitively to large amounts of glutamate.

claim_subject: Does the Orthopulse device accelerate the orthodontic correction of malocclusions?
scientific_truth: Poorly done studies show that the device can accelerate tooth movement in the short term. Whether this reduces the overall treatment time has not yet been sufficiently proven. The methodological weaknesses of the studies also mean that the results are not very credible. Possible side effects have not yet been sufficiently investigated.

claim_subject: Is it harmful for the mental development of the unborn child if the mother regularly eats fish contaminated with mercury during pregnancy?
scientific_truth: Many commercially available types of edible fish are contaminated with traces of methyl mercury. There are indications that regular consumption of such mercury-containing fish during pregnancy can impair the brain development of unborn children and thus their later mental abilities. In contrast, consumption of fish low in mercury could promote brain development in the unborn.

claim_subject: Can the consumption of caffeine during pregnancy harm the unborn child?
scientific_truth: There is insufficient evidence that moderate consumption of caffeinated beverages would have a negative impact on the child's development. Up to three cups of coffee a day does not appear to reduce the child's birth weight. Very large amounts of caffeine-containing beverages could possibly contribute to lower birth weight.

claim_subject: Are vegetables prepared in a microwave oven less healthy than those prepared in other ways?
scientific_truth: How vegetables change during preparation is extremely variable. With any type of heating, ingredients can be lost or become more easily accessible. In sum, it cannot be said that preparation in the microwave is always a bad choice.

claim_subject: Can garlic extract reduce high blood pressure and thus the risk of cardiovascular disease?
scientific_truth: Studies to date provide tentative evidence of a blood pressure-lowering effect of garlic. However, they are of too low quality to be able to prove a reduction in the risk of cardiovascular disease as a result of high blood pressure.

claim_subject: Can fructose damage the liver?
scientific_truth: There is no conclusive evidence for a possible liver-damaging effect of fructose.

claim_subject: Can green tea affect the likelihood of dying early and reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease?
scientific_truth: There is a lack of conclusive studies on the health effects of specific matcha. However, there is some evidence that green tea in general may reduce the likelihood of dying prematurely, especially from cardiovascular disease.

claim_subject: Is matcha tea particularly healthy?
scientific_truth: There is a lack of conclusive studies on the health effects of specific matcha. However, there is some evidence that green tea in general may reduce the likelihood of dying prematurely, especially from cardiovascular disease.

claim_subject: Can acupuncture prevent migraines and tension headaches?
scientific_truth: In the case of migraine, the preventive effect of acupuncture is probably similar to that of prophylactic medication. However, for both migraine and tension headaches, acupuncture performs only slightly better than sham acupuncture. Whether the pricking of traditional acupuncture points plays a role is unclear.

claim_subject: Can green tea reduce the likelihood of dying from cancer ?
scientific_truth: The results of previous studies suggest that green tea cannot reduce the risk of dying from cancer.

claim_subject: Can plant sterols or foods with them reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease?
scientific_truth: Plant sterols do lower cholesterol levels. However, whether they also reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease has not been researched. Animal studies even provide evidence that plant sterols in large quantities could increase the risk of cardiovascular disease. Whether this also applies to humans has not been investigated.

claim_subject: Can too much iodine cause autoimmune thyroid disease and consequently hypothyroidism?
scientific_truth: Autoimmune thyroid disease appears to occur more frequently in individuals with high iodine consumption. Whether high levels of iodine actually cause this disease has not been conclusively determined.

claim_subject: Is the sweetener aspartame harmful to health?
scientific_truth: Health damage from aspartame is unlikely. This also applies to people who consume aspartame-sweetened foods and beverages in large quantities over a long period of time. However, in people suffering from the hereditary disease phenylketonuria (PKU), aspartame can cause nerve and brain damage.

claim_subject: Does coffee affect cancer death risk?
scientific_truth: Current evidence suggests that coffee consumption in general is neither protective nor detrimental to cancer death risk.

claim_subject: Do diets with primarily or exclusively uncooked foods have health benefits?
scientific_truth: In studies, we have not been able to find convincing evidence that raw foods provide health benefits over healthy diets that include cooked foods. On the contrary, there is also evidence of possible harm.

claim_subject: Can increased water consumption prevent migraines or other headaches?
scientific_truth: Whether drinking more water can prevent headaches cannot be answered satisfactorily on the basis of studies conducted to date. If there is an effect, however, it is likely to be very small.

claim_subject: Offer the following herbal appetite suppressants effective and safe weight loss support: Devil's Tongue (Konjac Root), Caralluma fimbriata, Garcinia cambogia, Gymnea sylvestre, Ephedra, Irvinia gabonensis, Fenugreek, Hoodia gordonii, Common Bean, Bitter Orange?
scientific_truth: Due to the number of studies, it is unclear for a number of supposedly appetite-suppressing dietary supplements whether they can support successful weight loss. Well-done studies that run over a long period of time with a sufficient number of test subjects are scarce. Evidence for long-term safety and simultaneous efficacy is therefore lacking.

claim_subject: Are there health benefits to screening the general population for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) as a precaution?
scientific_truth: Even people with moderately severe COPD may have little health benefit from starting treatment as early as possible. People without symptoms who are diagnosed with COPD only as a result of a screening test are therefore unlikely to gain much health benefit from drug treatment.

claim_subject: Can cow's milk cause iron deficiency in babies in the first year of life?
scientific_truth: Cow's milk is low in usable iron. Therefore, cow's milk appears to increase the likelihood of iron deficiency in the blood of babies. It is unclear whether animal milk increases the risk of type 1 diabetes or blood in the stool, or reduces the likelihood of allergic diseases.

claim_subject: Does cow's milk for babies have other health disadvantages??
scientific_truth: Cow's milk is low in usable iron. Therefore, cow's milk appears to increase the likelihood of iron deficiency in the blood of babies. It is unclear whether animal milk increases the risk of type 1 diabetes or blood in the stool, or reduces the likelihood of allergic diseases.

claim_subject: Does drinking breast milk as a baby have a positive effect on later health and development?
scientific_truth: It is possible that children who have been exclusively breastfed for a long time are somewhat less likely to become overweight later on. There is also evidence that their IQ is slightly higher. However, it is difficult to isolate the influence of breast milk drinking. Therefore, it is questionable what significance the effects found have in practice.

claim_subject: Does Almased help with excess weight better than other diets?
scientific_truth: Those who reduce their calorie intake with the help of Almased lose weight. However, whether the product facilitates a diet or works better than other diets is not sufficiently studied.

claim_subject: Do products with talc, such as baby powder, increase the risk of ovarian cancer?
scientific_truth: Basically, cohort studies are more informative than case-control studies. The two existing large cohort studies speak against an increased risk, almost all case-control studies for an increased risk. In order not to underestimate a possible risk, we assess the study situation as unclear despite the cohort studies.

claim_subject: Do large portions, large plates or glasses, and larger packaging cause us to eat and drink more?
scientific_truth: The results of previous studies show that people generally seem to eat more and drink more (non-alcoholic) beverages when they are served larger portions. Whether smaller portions prevent obesity in the long term, however, has not been researched.

claim_subject: Does taking coconut oil improve mental abilities in dementia like Alzheimer's disease?
scientific_truth: We could find only one clinical study on the use of coconut oil in Alzheimer's disease. This was of such poor quality that no firm statement is possible.

claim_subject: Does the preparation "CAPS immu" from Ringana reduce the risk of infections in healthy people?
scientific_truth: Neither for the preparation itself nor for the individual components has such an effect been proven in clinical studies according to our research.

claim_subject: Do extracts from grape seeds have a health-promoting effect?
scientific_truth: The quality of studies available to date is too poor and the results are too contradictory to assess whether grape seed extract has a health-promoting effect.

claim_subject: Is the administration of magnesium through the skin effective?
scientific_truth: There are no well-done studies on this subject. Therefore, we lack reliable information as to whether or in what form magnesium can possibly penetrate the skin and then also have a (desired) effect.

claim_subject: Do kava kava supplements help with anxiety disorders?
scientific_truth: The fact that kava kava may slightly alleviate symptoms of an anxiety disorder is only weakly supported by studies. In addition, several cases of severe liver damage from preparations made from it are known in Europe and the USA.

claim_subject: Do ultrasound devices help against dust mites?
scientific_truth: Only dubiously published studies exist, the quality and significance of which cannot be assessed. Consequently, the effectiveness of the ultrasound devices is unclear.

claim_subject: Does the risk of food allergy decrease if babies are fed potentially allergenic foods (cow's milk, peanuts, chicken egg) as late as possible for the first time?
scientific_truth: in none of the clinical studies to date has the risk of food allergy decreased by feeding these foods as late as possible. Whether early supplementary feeding can reduce the risk is less clear, but possible at least for peanut allergy.

claim_subject: for fish, sesame, wheat?
scientific_truth: in none of the clinical studies to date has the risk of food allergy decreased by feeding these foods as late as possible. Whether early supplementary feeding can reduce the risk is less clear, but possible at least for peanut allergy.

claim_subject: Can willow bark tea help with inflammation, pain or fever?
scientific_truth: Significant, well-conducted studies are lacking on the effects of willow bark tea on pain, inflammation, or fever.

claim_subject: Can a supposedly "high acid" diet weaken bones?
scientific_truth: It is not likely that a supposedly "acid-rich" diet weakens the bones. There are no scientific studies on the effect on other diseases.

claim_subject: Does a supposedly "alkaline-rich" diet prevent chronic diseases?
scientific_truth: It is not likely that a supposedly "acid-rich" diet weakens the bones. There are no scientific studies on the effect on other diseases.

claim_subject: Can a blood test detect mental illness?
scientific_truth: Stress can certainly affect blood values, but conversely, we are not aware of any blood test that is actually useful for diagnosing mental illness.

claim_subject: Is surgery for an anterior cruciate ligament tear (by replacing the broken anterior cruciate ligament with tendon tissue from another part of the leg) followed by physical therapy better than physical therapy alone?
scientific_truth: No differences are found between the two treatment methods after either two or five years. However, this should be viewed with great caution. In a study on this, many patients in the group with physiotherapy had surgery after all within the next five years.

claim_subject: Can motherwort reduce migraine attacks?
scientific_truth: The existing studies differ greatly in their methods and the results are sometimes contradictory. According to the study with the most participants, motherwort can slightly reduce the number of migraine attacks per month.

claim_subject: Does metal in bed disturb sleep?
scientific_truth: Again and again consumers hear that bedsteads made of certain metals or with metal parts are harmful to health. But scientific studies on this are lacking. For this reason, we cannot say whether metal beds change the electrosmog exposure and thus perhaps even have a negative impact on health.

claim_subject: Does heat treatment (radiofrequency ablation or radiofrequency heat ablation of benign nodules of the thyroid gland work as well as conventional surgical methods?
scientific_truth: It is currently not clear whether this method achieves the same success as conventional surgical methods. The quality of the studies found is poor and leaves many questions about the effectiveness of the method unanswered. Possible undesirable side effects and long-term consequences are also unknown.

claim_subject: Does Imunoglukan strengthen the immune system?
scientific_truth: There are no studies that attest to Imunoglukan having a specific effect on a specific disease, nor any that confirm a general immune-boosting effect. The existing studies have glaring deficiencies.

claim_subject: Do cell phones promote the development and growth of tumors in the head?
scientific_truth: Despite intensive research, it is currently still unclear whether cell phones promote tumor diseases. According to current knowledge, the risk increases only minimally, if at all.

claim_subject: Does wearing bras promote breast cancer risk?
scientific_truth: The extent to which wearing bras affects breast cancer risk is poorly understood. So far, results of case-control studies tend to argue against a risk from bras, and there is no serious evidence that bras increase the risk.

claim_subject: Are tattoo inks harmful to health?
scientific_truth: Many tattoo inks contain substances that are harmful to health. Which colors can be used for tattoos without health concerns is unclear. There are no studies that investigate the risk.

claim_subject: Do plant hormones (phytoestrogens) other than genistein reduce the number and intensity of hot flashes during menopause?
scientific_truth: It is unclear whether phytoestrogens can help with hot flashes. Studies on this topic are often of modest quality; usually a comparison of the data is not possible. Therefore, an overall judgment cannot be made. One exception is the phytoestrogen genistein.

claim_subject: Does the herbal hormone genistein reduce the number and intensity of hot flashes during menopause???
scientific_truth: It is unclear whether phytoestrogens can help with hot flashes. Studies on this topic are often of modest quality; usually a comparison of the data is not possible. Therefore, an overall judgment cannot be made. One exception is the phytoestrogen genistein.

claim_subject: Does bloodletting according to Hildegard von Bingen have health benefits?
scientific_truth: Traditional bloodletting is based on ideas that have long been disproved and is not the subject of studies. However, in the case of very specific blood diseases, bloodletting is also used in scientific medicine.

claim_subject: Can FGXpress Power Strips reduce pain or improve wound healing?
scientific_truth: We could not find a single study on these patches - nor any reason to assume that they are effective.

claim_subject: Does treatment according to the fascial distortion model help with chronic shoulder pain?
scientific_truth: Currently, there is only one randomized controlled trial of this type of therapy. It suggests that fascia therapy may help with some shoulder conditions.

claim_subject: Are there effective alternatives to the breathing mask (CPAP) for sleep apnea?
scientific_truth: Although numerous other forms of treatment are available, some of them are too little researched or are clearly inferior to the standard therapy with CPAP.

claim_subject: Does closure of the foramen ovale prevent further strokes in people who have had a stroke of unknown cause?
scientific_truth: According to three large studies, closure of the patent foramen ovale can prevent another stroke better than purely drug treatment can.

claim_subject: Does stimulation current therapy (TENS - Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation) help with worn knee joints (knee osteoarthritis)?
scientific_truth: Whether TENS treatments can improve pain associated with knee osteoarthritis is unclear. In any case, it does not seem to be able to improve restrictions in everyday movements.

claim_subject: Does taking magnesium salts decrease the frequency and intensity of muscle cramps with unknown cause?
scientific_truth: No high-quality studies have been found on the efficacy of magnesium salts for exercise-induced muscle cramps, such as in athletes. For leg muscle cramps without an identifiable cause, researchers have been unable to demonstrate any effect of magnesium beyond placebo in studies. Pregnant women may benefit from magnesium supplements, but this evidence is not very robust.

claim_subject: Does taking magnesium salts reduce the frequency and intensity of exercise-induced muscle cramps during sports?
scientific_truth: No high-quality studies have been found on the efficacy of magnesium salts for exercise-induced muscle cramps, such as in athletes. For leg muscle cramps without an identifiable cause, researchers have been unable to demonstrate any effect of magnesium beyond placebo in studies. Pregnant women may benefit from magnesium supplements, but this evidence is not very robust.

claim_subject: Does taking magnesium salts reduce the frequency and intensity of muscle cramps in pregnancy?
scientific_truth: No high-quality studies have been found on the efficacy of magnesium salts for exercise-induced muscle cramps, such as in athletes. For leg muscle cramps without an identifiable cause, researchers have been unable to demonstrate any effect of magnesium beyond placebo in studies. Pregnant women may benefit from magnesium supplements, but this evidence is not very robust.

claim_subject: Does the active ingredient rivaroxaban (drug Xarelto) have a higher risk of dangerous bleeding than other anticoagulants?
scientific_truth: High-quality studies in the most common uses of rivaroxaban show either an equal or even lower risk of bleeding than other blood-clotting medications. However, this does not mean it is the best choice in all cases. Research is still needed for bleeding in the stomach or intestines.

claim_subject: Does vitamin D protect against dementia or memory loss?
scientific_truth: Some studies suggest a possible connection between the vitamin D concentration in the blood and a deteriorating memory or dementia. Whether vitamin D actually protects against memory deterioration or dementia remains open.

claim_subject: Does brain training boost intelligence?
scientific_truth: There are many ways of brain training, but no evidence that it can improve intelligence. The most research in science is about a specific training of the "working memory", here the studies speak against a general improvement of intelligence.

claim_subject: Does petroleum help against cancer?
scientific_truth: This rather absurd assumption has not been tested in studies. Since petroleum is more likely to pose a health hazard, such studies are also not conducted.

claim_subject: Does lavender scent help with sleep disorders?
scientific_truth: Based on the state of studies, it is unclear whether inhaling lavender aroma can help with sleep disorders. Most of the currently available studies have gross methodological flaws. In addition, it is uncertain what undesirable side effects may result from (long-term) inhalation of lavender aroma.

claim_subject: Does the drug Sovaldi (sofosbuvir) enable high cure rates for chronic hepatitis C?
scientific_truth: Yes, in combination with drugs that have been available for some time, cure rates of over 90 percent are possible with sofosbuvir. However, there are many different patient groups, and success rates are not the same for all.

claim_subject: Does alpha lipoic acid help prevent or treat Alzheimer's disease?
scientific_truth: It remains to be seen whether alpha lipoic acid can help prevent or delay the onset of Alzheimer's disease. There is also a lack of conclusive studies on the question of the extent to which the substance can favorably influence the course of a disease that has already broken out.

claim_subject: Are Vemma products good for health?
scientific_truth: We have found only one study that investigates health effects of Vemma. However, the study is so flawed that it does not allow us to draw any conclusions.

claim_subject: Do over-the-counter cough medicines relieve cough symptoms?
scientific_truth: That over-the-counter cough medicines provide relief from acute cough is neither proven nor disproven - there are simply no studies of sufficient quality to answer this question.

claim_subject: Does a diet rich in vitamin K2 protect against diseases of the cardiovascular system?
scientific_truth: While there are some studies that suggest a possible link between vitamin K2-rich diets and higher vascular health. However, the studies are not very conclusive.

claim_subject: Can shoe insoles relieve pain in people with high arches?
scientific_truth: Shoe insoles are often prescribed for foot malpositions. However, there are hardly any good studies on the effectiveness of these remedies. So for the time being, it remains largely unclear what orthopedic shoe insoles can do for people with foot malpositions and whether they relieve pain in the long term.

claim_subject: Can shoe insoles relieve pain in people with foot deformities other than high arch?
scientific_truth: Shoe insoles are often prescribed for foot malpositions. However, there are hardly any good studies on the effectiveness of these remedies. So for the time being, it remains largely unclear what orthopedic shoe insoles can do for people with foot malpositions and whether they relieve pain in the long term.

claim_subject: Can dowsers find harmful soil zones or water veins?
scientific_truth: Small studies show that dowsing rods cannot detect water veins or hypothetical interference zones in the ground.

claim_subject: Does bioresonance therapy help with health complaints?
scientific_truth: Good studies on the question are hard to find. Due to the lack of proof of efficacy, the risk of misdiagnosis and the lack of plausibility, professional associations have been warning against bioresonance for some time.

claim_subject: Do irradiations with cold red light help with chronic gingivitis?
scientific_truth: Previous studies indicate that chronic gingivitis and inflammation after dental surgery do not improve with irradiation with cold red light.

claim_subject: Does the Aspire system help you lose weight?
scientific_truth: Although there is only one small study on this, it shows a very large effect - which indicates that it is effective.

claim_subject: Can FLEXISEQ ointment relieve osteoarthritis pain?
scientific_truth: Comparisons to date with other commonly used treatments are difficult to interpret but do not yield clear evidence of efficacy.

claim_subject: Can butterbur prevent migraine attacks?
scientific_truth: Two well-done randomized-controlled trials show efficacy - the number of migraine attacks can probably be reduced with butterbur. Even if the effect is not huge, taking it may be worthwhile due to only minor side effects.

claim_subject: Does bisphenol A trigger allergies?
scientific_truth: Individual observational studies suggest an association between bisphenol A intake and the development of asthma, but not allergy, in early childhood. Asthma is often the consequence of allergy. However, the measurement of bisphenol A intake in these studies is too imprecise for a clear statement.

claim_subject: Can maggots accelerate the healing of chronic wounds compared to conventional treatment?
scientific_truth: Maggot therapy may not heal chronic wounds any faster than conventional wound care. However, the maggots seem to be able to clean the wound of dead tissue more quickly - but also cause more pain.

claim_subject: Do electric toothbrushes protect oral health better than manual brushes?
scientific_truth: Electric toothbrushes probably combat plaque and bleeding gums slightly better than conventional manual toothbrushes. The type of electric brush does not seem to play a major role.

claim_subject: Do antidepressants from the group of serotonin reuptake inhibitors help with depression?
scientific_truth: Serotonin reuptake inhibitors have been shown to be helpful in more severe depression, although the exact mechanisms are not clear. Overall, very strong or rapid effects are not expected. For milder depression, efficacy is more debatable.

claim_subject: Is there a health risk from metal contaminants in lipsticks?
scientific_truth: Several chemical analyses find traces of metals in lipsticks, which can in principle be harmful in high concentrations. However, the analyses do not examine the quantities in which the metals are actually absorbed and whether they cause damage in the body.

claim_subject: Can topiramate reduce the frequency of migraine attacks?
scientific_truth: Possibly yes. A review by the Cochrane Collaboration attests that topiramate slightly reduces the frequency of migraine attacks in adults, and in some patients the attacks even decrease significantly. Still, there are unanswered questions and the side effects should not be underestimated.

claim_subject: Does particulate matter pollution increase the risk of heart attack - even if the EU limits are complied with?
scientific_truth: Recent studies from Europe indicate that everyday exposure to particulate matter may increase the risk of acute heart disease (myocardial infarction, angina pectoris). General mortality may also be increased already by 'allowed' long-term exposure within the current EU limits.

claim_subject: Are endocrine disruptors in cosmetics a health risk?
scientific_truth: Although many cosmetics do indeed contain substances that can influence the hormone system, a health risk has not been proven. Ecological consequences, on the other hand, have already been demonstrated.

claim_subject: Can a dietary supplement containing omega-3 fatty acids, lipids, vitamins, and nutrients ("Souvenaid") noticeably slow or halt the decline of mental performance in Alzheimer's disease?
scientific_truth: Three randomized-controlled trials show that such a dietary supplement (Souvenaid®) is unlikely to markedly slow or halt the progression of Alzheimer's dementia. Taking omega-3 fatty acid or vitamin B supplements alone also does not appear to have such an effect.

claim_subject: Do vitamin E supplements increase the likelihood of early death?
scientific_truth: Studies on this topic are very inconsistent. Nevertheless, there is a possibility that vitamin E increases the risk of death. A meta-analysis warns against high-dose vitamin preparations.

claim_subject: Does meditation help against stress?
scientific_truth: Various forms of meditation seem to be able to alleviate stress both in healthy individuals and in people with mental illness. Studies on this are numerous, but the quality of the studies is consistently unsatisfactory.

claim_subject: Are there methods that effectively help against hormonal hair loss?
scientific_truth: Besides own hair transplantation, the active substances finasteride or minoxidil (as a solution) can help, but both agents have side effects. The effectiveness of other means is hardly or not secured.

claim_subject: Does eye training help prevent myopia?
scientific_truth: According to the current state of studies, an effectiveness of eye training can only be expected for very few diseases; an effect as prevention or therapy against myopia cannot be assumed at present.

claim_subject: Does Cryolipolysis cause noticeable body fat reduction?
scientific_truth: The effectiveness of cryolipolysis cannot be assessed objectively, as there are no scientific efficacy studies on it.

claim_subject: Is acupuncture for chronic pain more effective than placebo acupuncture treatment?
scientific_truth: Acupuncture is slightly superior to sham acupuncture treatment for some types of pain. However, pain patients are unlikely to notice this difference.

claim_subject: Can Internet-based self-help training based on cognitive behavioral therapy reduce the burden of tinnitus?
scientific_truth: Cognitive behavioral therapy can noticeably improve the quality of life and depressiveness of tinnitus sufferers. Internet-based self-help training based on cognitive behavioral therapy could be similarly helpful, but is often discontinued by sufferers.

claim_subject: Do probiotic foods have an antidepressant effect or a positive effect on the mind?
scientific_truth: Whether probiotics can help with depression or have a positive effect on the mood has never been investigated in clinical trials. In people with constipation, they could possibly improve mood.

claim_subject: Does treatment with radioactive agents help with pain in chronic inflammatory joint disease?
scientific_truth: Depending on the cause of the pain, radiosynoviorthesis can lead to considerable pain reduction, as confirmed by a 2009 review. However, it is not proven whether the treatment is more effective than cortisone treatment.

claim_subject: Does frequent porn use reduce gray matter volume in the brain?
scientific_truth: The study is not powered to examine the long-term effects of pornography on the brain and other studies on this were not found.

claim_subject: Can the active ingredient acetyl salicylic acid (ASA) protect against cancer?
scientific_truth: Taking ASA daily for several years seems to be able to reduce the risk of dying from cancer somewhat. However, it increases the risk of severe internal bleeding and stomach problems.

claim_subject: Is tick-borne tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) much milder in children than in adults?
scientific_truth: Current studies suggest that TBE is probably associated with milder symptoms in children than in adults. Permanent damage is also less frequent in younger patients. However, TBE can also have severe health consequences in children in individual cases.

claim_subject: Does treatment with cyanoacrylate (for example, Sapheon Venaseal™) help against varicose veins as well or better than other methods?
scientific_truth: To date, there are no results from clinical studies on this method. The efficacy in comparison with other treatments is therefore unclear.

claim_subject: Did oseltamivir (Tamiflu®) or other neuraminidase inhibitors help reduce deaths from the H1N1 influenza virus ("swine flu" virus)?
scientific_truth: Previously published analyses of data from the H1N1 influenza ("swine flu") pandemic period are of insufficient quality to answer this question.

claim_subject: Is aluminum intake responsible for the development of Alzheimer's disease?
scientific_truth: Scientific studies cannot prove with certainty a connection between the metal aluminum and the disease Alzheimer, but they cannot exclude it either.

claim_subject: Can regular exercise prevent or relieve migraine symptoms?
scientific_truth: In some, but not all, studies, regular exercise seems to at least somewhat reduce the pain intensity of future migraine attacks. Whether the frequency of migraine attacks can also be reduced cannot be assessed with certainty. for this, larger, better validated studies would have to be conducted.

claim_subject: Does less than 7h of sleep daily increase mental performance?
scientific_truth: Two small randomized-controlled studies indicate that mental performance decreases with the number of sleepless hours per night and the number of nights with insufficient sleep. No single scientific study provides evidence of an increase in mental performance due to shorter sleep duration.

claim_subject: Does regular intake of extra virgin olive oil protect against coronary heart disease such as heart attack?
scientific_truth: Regular consumption of cold-pressed olive oil may possibly prevent coronary heart disease. However, direct evidence is still pending.

claim_subject: Do frequent ejaculations have a protective effect against prostate cancer?
scientific_truth: A cohort study suggests that more frequent ejaculations starting at age 40, or over a lifetime, could potentially lower the risk of prostate cancer. This is not exclusive to ejaculations from masturbation, but from any sexual activity.

claim_subject: Does condom use cause depression in women?
scientific_truth: A study examining exactly this question was not found. Some scientific works with a broad question rather lead to the conclusion that there is no connection between depression and condom use.

claim_subject: Do today's children have a shorter life expectancy than their parents?
scientific_truth: Obesity and physical inactivity are increasing risk factors worldwide that can shorten life. In 2005, a study from the USA concluded that life expectancy could be reduced by 3 to 9 months when these risks were included.

claim_subject: Do rising temperatures and CO2 levels increase the risk of pollen allergy?
scientific_truth: Rising temperatures and increased CO2 concentrations cause plants to produce larger amounts of pollen over a longer period of time. However, it is unclear whether larger amounts of pollen and a longer pollen season increase the likelihood of developing pollen allergy.

claim_subject: Does training on vibration platforms cause a noticeable buildup of muscle strength?
scientific_truth: Vibration training may be helpful for building muscle strength in the legs, but it is not better than conventional training for this purpose. Whether the method is also suitable for weight reduction has not been sufficiently studied.

claim_subject: Does glucosamine prolong life?
scientific_truth: Although research here is still in its infancy and there is only one cohort study in humans besides basic studies, this shows possible effects. Further studies with better methods and other groups of participants are necessary.

claim_subject: Does Kinesio tape help in the treatment of joint and muscle injuries?
scientific_truth: There is no evidence that kinesio tape can reduce pain within a few days. It is unclear whether taping can help improve movement restrictions caused by an injury.

claim_subject: Do injections with Botulinum Toxin A (Botox®) help with urinary incontinence?
scientific_truth: Several small randomized-controlled trials show that injections of botulinum toxin A into the detrusor muscle surrounding the urinary bladder can reduce, but not completely prevent, the incidence of involuntary urinary leakage.

claim_subject: Can apigenin reduce cancer risk or prevent cancer progression?
scientific_truth: Studies suggest that even high levels of apigenin in food do not protect against cancer. In individual cases, it is suspected that apigenin in high amounts could weaken the effect of chemotherapy or even accelerate cancer growth.

claim_subject: Do generic drugs work as well as original drugs?
scientific_truth: Yes, the summarized results of clinical studies do not provide any evidence for a poorer efficacy of generics compared to originator drugs. However, comparative studies exist only for some agents against cardiovascular diseases and epilepsy.

claim_subject: Are animal-assisted therapies effective for mental illness?
scientific_truth: Studies on the effects of animal-assisted therapies are only partially conclusive. It seems plausible that animal-assisted therapies can be supportive for some mental illnesses; however, very large or rapid effects are unlikely.

claim_subject: Can lack of sleep cause obesity?
scientific_truth: People who regularly get too little sleep may be more likely to be overweight than those who get enough sleep. But whether lack of sleep itself causes obesity is unclear.

claim_subject: Is breaking an energy-saving lamp harmful to health?
scientific_truth: If an energy-saving lamp breaks, mercury vapor is released in quantities that can exceed the limits considered safe. Whether this can cause damage to health has not been directly investigated. However, after removal of the broken glass and good ventilation of the room, the value quickly falls back below the limit value.

claim_subject: Does copper intake increase the risk of Alzheimer's disease?
scientific_truth: Some studies claim to have found links between high copper levels and Alzheimer's disease. Whether copper intake actually has an impact on Alzheimer's risk is not clear.

claim_subject: Do air ions cause an improvement of allergies?
scientific_truth: Whether ionized air can reduce allergic symptoms is unclear, as no studies exist on this question. Air ionization devices do not appear to be effective against asthma in general.

claim_subject: Do air ions cause an improvement of asthma??
scientific_truth: Whether ionized air can reduce allergic symptoms is unclear, as no studies exist on this question. Air ionization devices do not appear to be effective against asthma in general.

claim_subject: Do smoking bans lead to fewer preterm births?
scientific_truth: A large review shows a 10% reduced risk of preterm birth. Due to some limitations, the evidence is nevertheless low, further studies from different countries will probably soon bring clarity.

claim_subject: Do special garments with the active ingredient Liporeductyl help against cellulite?
scientific_truth: There are only small studies that neither stand up to methodological criteria nor have been scientifically published. Sustained efficacy has not been proven, which, according to the current status, applies to all common remedies against cellulite.

claim_subject: Does alcohol in moderate amounts prolong life?
scientific_truth: In moderate amounts, alcohol could reduce the likelihood of dying prematurely. In higher doses, however, it clearly increases this risk. This is unclear for caffeine.

claim_subject: Does caffeine make us die sooner???
scientific_truth: In moderate amounts, alcohol could reduce the likelihood of dying prematurely. In higher doses, however, it clearly increases this risk. This is unclear for caffeine.

claim_subject: Does light freezing help with weight loss?
scientific_truth: Some laboratory studies show that the body reacts to colder temperatures with higher energy consumption and burns more fat. Nevertheless, it is completely unclear whether this supports weight loss; that is, whether the process is strong enough and whether other mechanisms do not work against it. Weight loss through freezing has not been investigated in clinical studies.

claim_subject: Does acupuncture help against hay fever?
scientific_truth: We have not found any meaningful studies that can provide evidence of improvement in hay fever.

claim_subject: Do earrings cause discomfort by destroying acupuncture points or meridians?
scientific_truth: Earrings very often lead to complications, fortunately most of them are harmless. However, whether earrings can also destroy meridians or similar representation points of body regions in the auricle and thus lead to health complaints has not been investigated in studies.

claim_subject: Does the "Rolfing" treatment cause an improvement of body malpositions as well as certain pains?
scientific_truth: The few studies on "Rolfing" are too inconclusive to answer the question.

claim_subject: Does marijuana use reduce the risk of developing diabetes?
scientific_truth: Two cross-sectional studies provide evidence for a diabetes-preventive effect of active ingredients from the cannabis plant. That the consumption of marijuana actually reduces the risk of diabetes has yet to be confirmed by extensive studies.

claim_subject: Do fish oil capsules promote prostate cancer?
scientific_truth: In general, there seems to be a negative effect of omega-3 fatty acids in fish oil capsules: DHA and EPA in high doses could increase the risk of prostate cancer. However, the results should be viewed with caution. Other, still unknown factors could also play an important role.

claim_subject: Does virgin conception exist?
scientific_truth: To date, only one study has been conducted on this issue. The scientific evidence based on this study does not allow a clear answer.

claim_subject: Are movement exercises useful for back pain?
scientific_truth: Exercise reduces the risk of getting back pain again and can relieve chronic back pain somewhat. However, quick relief from acute pain is not to be expected.

claim_subject: Does taking the birth control pill adversely affect mate choice? (Reader inquiry)
scientific_truth: Even though individual studies find a slight correlation between taking the pill and choosing a partner, there is no evidence that it negatively affects partner choice.

claim_subject: Does UV light reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease?
scientific_truth: It is theoretically conceivable that UVB light could reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease. However, studies published so far cannot sufficiently confirm this assumption.

claim_subject: Is the Gynefix® contraceptive necklace as effective for contraception as the birth control pill or the "IUD"?
scientific_truth: The 6-link copper-containing contraceptive necklace Gynefix® is comparable in contraceptive effectiveness to other copper-containing intrauterine devices ("IUDs"). A comparison with the contraceptive effectiveness of the contraceptive pill is not satisfactorily possible based on our research.

claim_subject: Can coenzyme Q10 lead to a rejuvenation of the skin's appearance?
scientific_truth: Since there are no studies on this subject conducted according to common scientific standards, this question cannot be answered.

claim_subject: Is there an increased risk of long-term effects on the unborn child with chemotherapy starting in the 2nd trimester of pregnancy?
scientific_truth: Studies published to date do not suggest a greatly increased risk of adverse effects on the child, but such a risk cannot be ruled out.

claim_subject: Can regular screening significantly reduce the risk of dying from prostate cancer?
scientific_truth: The regular PSA screening test can hardly reduce the risk of death from prostate cancer. In fact, it often leads to overdiagnosis with serious consequences such as incontinence and erectile dysfunction.

claim_subject: Does removal and examination of the first lymph nodes after the prostate is affected by cancer (sentinel lymph nodes or sentinel lymph nodes) improve the chances of cure? (Reader Inquiry)
scientific_truth: Removal and examination of sentinel lymph nodes helps assess the progression of prostate cancer. However, whether it improves the chances of cure cannot be said due to the low level of scientific evidence.

claim_subject: Can a treatment with singing bowls relieve pain?
scientific_truth: Singing bowl therapy does not appear to be effective for relieving pain.

claim_subject: Is the HIV saliva self-test, which is about to be approved in the U.S., as reliable as a laboratory test or a rapid test at the doctor's office?
scientific_truth: The aforementioned HIV self-test of saliva samples is significantly less accurate than a standard laboratory blood test. Relatively likely, it is also more inaccurate when self-performed than a rapid saliva or blood test performed by a physician.

claim_subject: Does religion promote mental health?
scientific_truth: The studies do not allow any conclusion to be drawn for several reasons: the results are contradictory, only a few studies are by independent authors, and religion is not a concept that is measured uniformly; neither effects nor side effects can be clearly attributed to the factor "religion" because there is no such thing as a uniform factor "religion."

claim_subject: Do braces treatments have preventive medical benefits in addition to aesthetic ones?
scientific_truth: The long-term effects of tooth straightening are still very poorly researched. Apart from obvious effects in extreme malocclusions, there is no good evidence for either medical benefit or high risk.

claim_subject: What are the advantages and disadvantages of vaccinating infants simultaneously with the usual six-dose vaccine (against diphtheria, tetanus, polio, pertussis, hepatitis B, and Haemophilus influenzae B) and a pneumococcal vaccine? (Reader inquiry)
scientific_truth: Simultaneous vaccination with pneumococcal and six-way vaccine results in essentially equivalent protection against the 6 pathogens compared with six-way vaccination alone. The somewhat increased risk of fever after vaccination is offset by additional, nearly complete protection against pneumococcal infection and infection.

claim_subject: Does the use of laptops with active WLAN (wireless internet access) affect sperm quality in men?
scientific_truth: The underlying study is not sufficiently conclusive to be able to determine such an effect. Currently, there is no high-quality scientific study that has investigated this issue.

claim_subject: Can phthalates cause diabetes?
scientific_truth: Studies conducted in humans to date show that people with diabetes or pre-diabetes have significantly elevated phthalate concentrations in their bodies. Although these studies cannot prove that diabetes is caused or contributed to by phthalates, results from laboratory studies in the test tube and in animals point in this direction.

claim_subject: Does staining brain tumors with the dye aminolevulinic acid before surgery help patients survive longer?
scientific_truth: Surgery of brain tumors stained with aminolevulinic acid is more complete than without staining. Although the tumor returned in fewer patients in the initial period after surgery, it is unclear whether the long-term survival rate is also greater.

claim_subject: Can exercise prevent premature deaths from heart attacks, strokes, heart failure, and pre-diabetes as effectively as medication?
scientific_truth: An evaluation of several meta-analyses provides evidence that exercise can prevent premature death after stroke. After heart attacks or in cases of pre-diabetes, exercise appears to be similarly effective to the corresponding drugs. In the case of heart failure, however, medication is likely to be more effective.

claim_subject: Can taking the enzyme diamino oxidase prevent alcohol-related hangover symptoms?
scientific_truth: Such an effect is not likely, nor do clinical studies exist on this issue.

claim_subject: Can an anti-oxidant such as pseudocatalase stop or reverse hair graying?
scientific_truth: This question has not yet been scientifically investigated and therefore cannot be answered.

claim_subject: Can sexual activity relieve headaches?
scientific_truth: Individuals report subjective improvement. However, reliable scientific evidence that sexual activity in general can relieve migraine and cluster headaches is insufficient.

claim_subject: Does transcranial direct current stimulation help against severe depression?
scientific_truth: A brand new review shows that tDCS does not lead to lasting improvement in patients with major depression, nor is the response to therapy better than to placebo treatment. However, the number of participants, both overall and in the individual studies, is too low for a reliable assessment.

claim_subject: Is the success of conventional treatment of a herniated disc equivalent to that of disc surgery?
scientific_truth: Disc surgery leads to faster pain relief in the short term, but in most cases is unlikely to bring any long-term benefit compared to conventional therapy. It is also more expensive and somewhat riskier.

claim_subject: Does regular use of sleeping pills promote the risk of death or cancer?
scientific_truth: There is a connection between the use of sleeping pills and an increased risk of death or cancer. However, it cannot be ruled out with certainty that other reasons are not responsible for this increased risk.

claim_subject: Does increased time outdoors inhibit myopia in children?
scientific_truth: There is probably a correlation between reduced myopia and outdoor activities. However, it is not possible to say beyond doubt whether increased time spent outdoors is actually the cause of reduced myopia. Various other factors also play a role in the development of myopia.

claim_subject: Do household cleaners and room fresheners in spray form cause damage to the heart?
scientific_truth: There is evidence that people who often use household sprays more often have asymptomatic abnormalities of the heart rhythm. However, whether these abnormalities will later lead to disease, and whether household sprays are actually the cause, remains to be determined by larger and longer studies.

claim_subject: Can exercise improve mental performance impaired by alcohol consumption?
scientific_truth: There are only two studies that deal with this issue. Only one examines the problem in humans, and that is only a small pilot study. Whether sport reduces alcohol-related brain damage has not been clarified.

claim_subject: Can over-the-counter combination medications help with tension headache and migraine better than medications containing only single active ingredients?
scientific_truth: The addition of caffeine may slightly increase the effect of common painkillers in some people. The combination of acetylsalicylic acid (ASA), paracetamol and caffeine is possibly the most effective. However, no better tolerability of the combination preparations was found. However, no comparative data are yet available for several other active ingredients or combinations of active ingredients.

claim_subject: Does hyperthermia treatment support chemotherapy in fighting cancer? (anonymous request with link to the Standard article)
scientific_truth: There are indications that hyperthermia can increase survival rates in some types of cancer. Overall, there are still too few large studies available to be able to make definite statements.

claim_subject: Can stress promote dementia?
scientific_truth: There is evidence that chronic stress in work and private life may increase the risk of dementia in old age. However, this needs to be confirmed by larger studies. However, stress is only one of many possible influences.

claim_subject: Does the risk for the unborn child to develop asthma later on increase if the mother is exposed to high pollen concentrations during pregnancy?
scientific_truth: It is not clear whether a child later has an increased risk of asthma if its mother has contact with large amounts of pollen during pregnancy. Studies to date on this are rare and in some cases show methodological weaknesses. Studies conducted according to strict criteria would be necessary to answer this question unequivocally.

claim_subject: Are children conceived in May more likely to be born prematurely than children conceived in other months?
scientific_truth: There are indications that children conceived in May are born prematurely. The reason for this could be the flu, which hits May babies the hardest. The temperature can also influence the time of birth.

claim_subject: Does osteopathy work?
scientific_truth: For some therapies that fit under the broad term osteopathy, the evidence of studies indicates efficacy for back pain and some forms of headache; however, evidence of efficacy is lacking for many forms of osteopathy.

claim_subject: Do creams with sterol compounds improve the appearance of cellulite skin?
scientific_truth: There is no evidence for such an effect.

claim_subject: For women at high risk of breast cancer, does a precautionary mastectomy make more sense than regular participation in intensive screening?
scientific_truth: High-risk patients can significantly reduce their risk of breast cancer with preventive breast screening. Nevertheless, no general recommendation can be derived from this, as intensive screening programs are an alternative. However, good long-term studies are still lacking for both preventive measures, and the decision can only be made on a very individual basis.

claim_subject: Does tocilizumab specifically help children with rheumatoid arthritis (juvenile idiopathic arthritis) ?
scientific_truth: In contrast to adult rheumatoid arthritis patients, where the efficacy of tocilizumab has been well studied, there are only 2 controlled studies for use in children on a specific subtype (systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis) with very few participants. These suggest better efficacy than in adults, but in reality this is likely to be lower than presented in the study results.

claim_subject: Does the Toxoplasma gondii parasite affect suicide rates?
scientific_truth: Meanwhile, some studies show a link between infection with the protozoan T. gondii and a higher suicide rate. However, it is not yet clear whether the parasite actually has an influence, because a third factor is also conceivable that influences both the infection rate and the suicide rate.

claim_subject: Is Exemestane better than other hormone-altering drugs for reducing the risk of breast cancer or treating it?
scientific_truth: The group of so-called aromatase inhibitors, which includes Exemestane, causes a higher survival rate in the treatment of breast cancer patients than other hormone-influencing drugs. Exemestane probably does not work any better than the aromatase inhibitor anastrozole. Whether Exemestane works better compared to other aromatase inhibitors is still unclear.

claim_subject: Does a newly approved contraceptive pill with the active ingredient combination nomegestrol acetate and 17ß-estradiol have fewer undesirable side effects than other birth control pills?
scientific_truth: Compared to two other birth control pills available in pharmacies, side effects such as acne, weight gain or headaches occur just as often or even more frequently with the newly approved pill.

claim_subject: Does PrEP reduce the risk of HIV infection?
scientific_truth: Studies to date have confirmed the preventive effect. People who take PrEP medication correctly have a significantly lower risk of HIV infection. However, infection cannot be completely ruled out.

claim_subject: Does exercise, a restricted diet, or both together help prevent excessive weight gain during pregnancy?
scientific_truth: The summarized results of previous studies clearly show this. However, it is less well established that the measures also improve the health of mother and child during pregnancy and birth.

claim_subject: Does taking antibiotics for acute sinusitis speed up the healing of the infection?
scientific_truth: Taking antibiotics can somewhat speed up the healing of an acute sinus infection. However, the success rate is not exhilarating: antibiotics lead to a faster recovery in only 5 out of 100 people. Pain and impairment in everyday life are not improved. And, of course, antibiotics can cause side effects.

claim_subject: Does colonoscopy reduce mortality from colorectal cancer?
scientific_truth: For the small colonoscopy (sigmoidoscopy) an effectiveness is well proven, whether the large colonoscopy (colonoscopy) works even better is not proven. It is not possible that colorectal cancer could be prevented entirely.

claim_subject: Do nicotine replacement products like nicotine gum or nicotine patches help with long-term smoking cessation?
scientific_truth: The benefits of nicotine replacement have been proven in numerous studies. Compared to a placebo, more people manage not to smoke after six months or longer. The success can even be increased somewhat by additional support (counseling, talks).

claim_subject: Is short, high-intensity training equally effective as longer, moderate-intensity training?
scientific_truth: Yes, possibly. However, there are only a few studies on this, some of which are inadequate. Possible side effects have not been studied.

claim_subject: Do behavioral therapy methods help with specific fears (phobias) such as fear of spiders?
scientific_truth: Yes, the most effective method is confrontation therapy. Patients are confronted with the fear-inducing stimulus (e.g., a spider) more and more until they have become accustomed to it.

claim_subject: Can honey accelerate the healing of second degree burns with pain, redness and blisters?
scientific_truth: With honey, moderately severe burns that affect the uppermost layers of the skin and can also lead to wound infections heal four to five days faster than with conventional burn treatments. Whether honey also provides benefits for small, fresh wounds is insufficiently researched.

claim_subject: Does honey heal small, fresh wounds faster than the usual wound treatment?
scientific_truth: With honey, moderately severe burns that affect the uppermost layers of the skin and can also lead to wound infections heal four to five days faster than with conventional burn treatments. Whether honey also provides benefits for small, fresh wounds is insufficiently researched.

claim_subject: Does honey work better than other wound treatments for chronic wounds (open leg, diabetic foot)?
scientific_truth: With honey, moderately severe burns that affect the uppermost layers of the skin and can also lead to wound infections heal four to five days faster than with conventional burn treatments. Whether honey also provides benefits for small, fresh wounds is insufficiently researched.

claim_subject: Does sitting for long periods despite compensatory exercise increasingly lead to type 2 diabetes?
scientific_truth: Prolonged sitting and an inactive lifestyle lead to a significantly increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Exercise has a beneficial effect in the prevention of diabetes. Whether physical activity can completely offset the risk of a predominantly sedentary lifestyle, or the extent to which this would be necessary, is not clear from the available studies.

claim_subject: Do acupuncture or related smoking cessation methods help you stay smoke-free for at least 6 months?
scientific_truth: There is no evidence for a long-lasting success of smoking cessation with the help of acupuncture or similar methods. In the short term, acupuncture might help slightly. Overall, however, acupuncture is clearly inferior to nicotine replacement therapy.

claim_subject: Do gastrointestinal surgeries (bariatric surgeries) improve symptoms of type 2 diabetes?
scientific_truth: Gastrointestinal surgery significantly improves diabetes symptoms in the majority of overweight patients with type 2 diabetes. However, these operations are associated with risks. Other methods (such as exercise programs or weight reduction without surgery) are effective to a lesser extent, but are far less risky.

claim_subject: Is there a connection between ADHD and neurodermatitis?
scientific_truth: Several large studies show that there is a link between ADHD and neurodermatitis. Whether one disease is the cause of the other or whether both diseases have common causes is not yet clear.

claim_subject: Can injections with the enzyme collagenase straighten fingers bent by Dupuytren's disease without surgery? (Reader inquiry)
scientific_truth: Collagenase injections can straighten the fingers, but success does not always occur and is usually - as with the usual surgery - not permanent. Almost all patients experience undesirable side effects, which can also be severe in individual cases.

claim_subject: Do mindfulness-based methods effect improvement in chronic pain?
scientific_truth: Some clinical studies suggest an efficacy of mindfulness-based methods for pain management, but several other studies cannot confirm such an effect. A definitive answer could come from studies with a larger number of participants.

claim_subject: Does high air pollution increase the risk for the unborn to develop autism later in life?
scientific_truth: There may be a link between the increased incidence of autism and air pollution during pregnancy. However, previous studies have been too imprecise to actually identify air pollution as a cause of autism. The possible risk should be clarified by more detailed studies.

claim_subject: Is it harmful to health to eat apple cores with the apple?
scientific_truth: Normally, apple cores pass through the body undigested. Even if they are bitten, not enough poison enters the body to pose a danger.

claim_subject: Can taking selenium prevent cancer?
scientific_truth: The summarized results of studies conducted so far reliably show that selenium preparations do not protect against cancer. However, the dose at which selenium becomes harmful to the body is insufficiently researched.

claim_subject: Does mesotherapy help against pain?
scientific_truth: Mesotherapy is an umbrella term for very different treatments that have only the method of administration in common, namely the injection of many small doses of an agent into a specific skin layer. Therefore, it is not possible to make a general statement about its effectiveness.

claim_subject: Do general health checkups lead to longer life?
scientific_truth: Health screenings for adults from the general population do not have the hoped-for effect: participants do not live longer as a result of serial screening and preventive care.

claim_subject: Can dementia be prevented?
scientific_truth: It is possible that sport and exercise, mentally demanding activities, a busy social life and a Mediterranean diet could prevent dementia. It is possible that diabetes, smoking, depression, loneliness, head injuries and pesticides increase the risk of dementia. However, all these factors are not well established.

claim_subject: Does the plant pigment beta-carotene protect against cancer?
scientific_truth: There is no evidence of a cancer risk-reducing effect for beta-carotene. On the contrary, beta-carotene preparations may even increase the risk of bladder cancer and cancer in smokers.

claim_subject: Can vitamin supplements protect against life-threatening diseases such as cancer or cardiovascular disease?
scientific_truth: Antioxidant and multivitamin supplements do not reduce the likelihood of dying prematurely from cancer, cardiovascular disease, or other causes. Taking beta-carotene and possibly vitamin E may actually increase the likelihood of premature death. The only exception is vitamin D supplements; they are likely to have a small life-prolonging effect in the elderly.

claim_subject: Is it true that lowering cholesterol does not reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease?
scientific_truth: No. High cholesterol, along with other risk factors, can increase the likelihood of cardiovascular disease. If the proportion of "bad" LDL cholesterol in the blood is lowered (with medication or through a change in diet), the risk of diseases such as heart attack or stroke also decreases.

claim_subject: Do static magnets help against pain?
scientific_truth: Both a somewhat older review and several high-quality randomized controlled trials show that magnets do not work better than sham treatment.

claim_subject: Does hypnosis help with chronic bowel problems?
scientific_truth: Since 1984, studies have shown a success of hypnosis against intestinal complaints. However, the studies have only been conducted on small groups of patients and also show methodological weaknesses. Thus, there is only little evidence of efficacy.

claim_subject: Does taking vitamin D supplements during pregnancy increase the risk of food allergy for the unborn child?
scientific_truth: Whether vitamin D supplements can increase the risk of food allergy in the unborn child is unclear, as studies on this issue have yielded conflicting results.

claim_subject: Is combined hormone therapy with estrogen and progestin safe for women in late menopause (after the last menstrual period)?
scientific_truth: Hormone therapy with estrogen- and progestin-containing preparations makes women more likely to suffer a stroke or heart attack. The risk of breast cancer is also increased. The hormone drugs probably protect a little against diabetes, colon cancer or bone fractures. However, they are no good as a preventive medicine because of the list of side effects.

claim_subject: Can negative expectancy reduce the effect of pain medications?
scientific_truth: Studies clearly show that ineffective placebo can bring severe side effects, depending on the patient's expectations. One effect can also be that the effectiveness of painkillers is limited.

claim_subject: Is sex as good an endurance workout as running?
scientific_truth: Studies show that physical exertion during sex is present but rather moderate. Compared with targeted exercise, the energy expenditure is lower.

claim_subject: Can electrical brain stimulation reduce the amount of food eaten?
scientific_truth: Electrical brain stimulation may be able to reduce short-term cravings for high-calorie foods. However, it is unclear that the treated persons actually eat less of them; study results on this are contradictory.

claim_subject: Are plastic kitchen boards more hygienic than wooden ones?
scientific_truth: Whether wooden boards in the kitchen have hygienic disadvantages is unclear. Previous studies on this are too contradictory to answer this question clearly.

claim_subject: Does excessive beer or alcohol consumption lead to obesity?
scientific_truth: In some studies, alcohol consumption does seem to be related to weight gain. In other studies, however, there is either no effect or even the opposite effect. The study situation is contradictory.

claim_subject: Do omega-3 fatty acids or a diet rich in fish help with rheumatoid arthritis?
scientific_truth: According to the majority of studies, preparations with omega-3 fatty acids cannot improve pain and other symptoms in rheumatoid arthritis. However, the results are sometimes contradictory. The effectiveness of preparations made from the New Zealand green-lipped mussel is also unclear. Whether a diet rich in fish helps is insufficiently studied.

claim_subject: Does unprocessed red meat increase the risk of cardiovascular disease?
scientific_truth: Whether unprocessed red meat increases the likelihood of cardiovascular disease is unclear, and study results are conflicting. However, processed red meat such as ham, bacon or sausages could increase the risk.

claim_subject: Does processed red meat (sausages, ham, bacon) increase the risk of cardiovascular disease???
scientific_truth: Whether unprocessed red meat increases the likelihood of cardiovascular disease is unclear, and study results are conflicting. However, processed red meat such as ham, bacon or sausages could increase the risk.

claim_subject: Does hawthorn extract help patients with heart muscle weakness (heart failure)?
scientific_truth: The results of the studies found differ significantly and leave more questions open than they answer.

claim_subject: Is glyphosate carcinogenic?
scientific_truth: Depending on how much animal experiments and laboratory tests are weighted against studies on humans, one arrives at different assessments. With regard to human studies, we consider the question to be unresolved at present.

claim_subject: Does psychotherapy help with burnout?
scientific_truth: Of the psychotherapy modalities, only Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) has evidence of potential efficacy for burnout. For other forms of psychotherapy, the scientific evidence is unclear or non-existent.

claim_subject: Is electrical muscle stimulation (EMS) in combination with ordinary fitness training more efficient than fitness training alone?
scientific_truth: There is evidence for the principle effectiveness of EMS for muscle strengthening. For a superiority of the combination of EMS and ordinary training compared to fitness training alone, the evidence is contradictory.

claim_subject: Can vitamin and nutrient supplements prevent the eye disease age-related macular degeneration?
scientific_truth: Vitamin E and beta-carotene cannot prevent the development of age-related macular degeneration. However, in combination with zinc and vitamin C, they probably allow certain forms of an existing disease to progress somewhat more slowly.

claim_subject: Can they delay the progression of eye disease?
scientific_truth: Vitamin E and beta-carotene cannot prevent the development of age-related macular degeneration. However, in combination with zinc and vitamin C, they probably allow certain forms of an existing disease to progress somewhat more slowly.

claim_subject: Do milk or dairy products promote colon cancer and rectal cancer?
scientific_truth: It is likely that dairy products reduce the risk of colon and rectal cancer, and possibly bladder cancer. However, very large amounts of milk & dairy products could possibly increase the risk of prostate cancer. It should be remembered that about the same number of men die from colon and rectal cancer as from prostate cancer.

claim_subject: Does yoga change the genetic makeup?
scientific_truth: Yoga - like any other physical activity - can influence the activity of genes. But the genes themselves are not changed by it.

claim_subject: Which of the three most common laser eye surgeries produces the best results and has the fewest side effects?
scientific_truth: If only new studies are considered, all three techniques are equally successful. Probable advantages of LASIK: less pain after surgery and good vision more quickly.

claim_subject: Can electromagnetic fields with a specific pattern (pulsed electromagnetic fields, PEMF) heal injuries?
scientific_truth: No good injury studies can be found on the device. The only randomized-controlled study treats fatigue in patients with the incurable nerve disease multiple sclerosis and is not very conclusive. Even for the whole range of similar treatment methods, there is no sufficient evidence of efficacy.

claim_subject: Does the drug fingolimod reduce the progression of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis similarly or better than previous drugs?
scientific_truth: Two manufacturer-funded clinical trials attest Fingolimod such efficacy that exceeds that of interferon beta therapy. However, the drug can also cause serious side effects.

claim_subject: Can cancer be successfully fought with intentionally induced fever?
scientific_truth: In the early 20th century, cancer was indeed sometimes fought with fever, sometimes successfully. But the therapies and trials are poorly documented and were risky. An assessment of efficacy is not possible based on the studies to date.

claim_subject: Can some forms of headache be successfully treated with heat?
scientific_truth: Heat on tense muscles is pleasant, but no evidence exists that the tension is released and the headache is relieved.

claim_subject: Does electro-acupuncture on the ear help against pain?
scientific_truth: Electro-ear acupuncture could be supportive against chronic pain such as neck or low back pain. The method cannot completely replace painkillers. For surgery-related pain, the effectiveness is uncertain.

claim_subject: Does treatment with the new drug erenumab reduce the number of migraine days per month?
scientific_truth: In five studies available to date, which tend to be shorter, participants suffered from migraine less frequently with erenumab than with a placebo. The studies were of high methodological quality. In episodic migraine, people "saved" about 1 to 2 migraine days per month . For chronic migraine, sufferers had about 2.5 fewer days of pain per month.

claim_subject: Is screening by optical coherence tomography superior to conventional examinations for the early detection of diabetic macular edema?
scientific_truth: No, screening by optical coherence tomography alone is too inaccurate. An examination using an ophthalmoscope and pupil dilating eye drops or with the help of fundus photography is a safer method.

claim_subject: Does the treatment of diabetes-related retinal diseases by injection of VEGF inhibitors provide an advantage compared to conventional laser treatment?
scientific_truth: There is evidence of better short-term efficacy for VEGF inhibitor injections compared with laser coagulation, but the method is insufficiently studied. Whether the effect is safe in the long term and effective at the same time is unclear.

claim_subject: Do saw palmetto preparations help with benign prostate enlargement?
scientific_truth: Many men with benign prostate enlargement turn to herbal remedies. However, current evidence for reliable and long-term efficacy is generally lacking, and most remedies are not well studied. It is therefore not possible to lump all products together.

claim_subject: Do plant extracts of African plum tree, beta-sitosterol or ryegrass pollen extract (Cernilton) help benign prostate enlargement?
scientific_truth: Many men with benign prostate enlargement turn to herbal remedies. However, current evidence for reliable and long-term efficacy is generally lacking, and most remedies are not well studied. It is therefore not possible to lump all products together.

claim_subject: Does not wearing bras provide medical benefits?
